composite_aspect_frame.conjunction:
In a composite chart a conjunction is not a blend of two things but a third thing.

Oken's image is two expensive perfumes poured into one vial: what comes out is a new compound, and neither original can be recovered from it. The two principles do not negotiate here and the pair cannot address one without the other - this is a single fused function of the bond, and the area of life it governs carries a concentrated gravity the relationship cannot step outside of. Whatever else the chart says, this is where the couple is obliged to act as one force.
composite_aspect_frame.opposition:
In a composite chart an opposition is an axis the relationship holds open, and the partners take turns carrying its ends.

Both ends belong to the bond rather than one to each person - but with two bodies in the room the pair will always distribute them, one voicing the freedom and the other drafted into playing the brake. The seats get swapped over the years; the tension does not. That is the structural feature, and it is not a fault: an opposition gives a relationship a sharp reflective awareness of its own dynamics that no other aspect supplies. What ruins it is either partner believing the role they are currently holding is who they are.
composite_aspect_frame.square:
In a composite chart a square is the friction the relationship runs on, and it does not get solved.

Two of the bond's own functions want incompatible things, so the tension keeps generating events instead of resolving into anything. This is the recurring argument the pair will still be having in twenty years, and the honest work is to use it as an engine rather than wait for it to end. A couple that refuses the friction does not escape it - the relationship somatises what goes unexpressed and it arrives later as a sudden domestic blowup with no obvious cause.
composite_aspect_frame.trine:
In a composite chart a trine is something the relationship does well without trying, and that is exactly its danger.

Two functions of the bond agree, and the ease is real. It is also a closed system - Greene's point is that a trine loops back on itself, generating nothing and asking nothing. Oken warns that too many of them retard a relationship into a Lotus Eater temperament with no motive to develop. The specific trap in a composite chart is that the couple will retreat into their trines to avoid the work their squares are demanding, which is how a partnership can feel effortless and go nowhere for a decade.
composite_aspect_frame.quincunx:
In a composite chart a quincunx is a mismatch the relationship cannot reconcile, only translate.

The two placements share no element, mode or polarity and traditionally cannot see one another at all - so unlike a square there is nothing to fight and unlike an opposition there is no clean see-saw to balance. These are two parts of the bond speaking different languages, and the only thing that works is continuous deliberate translation: saying the thing out loud because the relationship's blueprint provides no automatic bridge between these two functions. The adjustment never completes, and a couple that expects it to will read the permanent effort as evidence of failure.
